card.name: Words just before 'with' in drug combinations
card.fires_on: The word right before an expected 'with' or 'in combination with' naming another drug, such as incompatible, coadministered, mixed in, or taken in. It also fires on 'in a relationship with'.

modes.label: Incompatible with
modes.description: The word incompatible after 'physically' or 'be', before a list of drugs.
modes.example: Rocuronium bromide injection is physically<< incompatible>> when mixed with the following drugs: am

modes.label: Coadministered with
modes.description: The ending of coadministered or co-administered, before 'with' and a drug name.
modes.example: No dosage adjustment of anidulafungin is needed when it is co-administer<<ed>> with rifampin [see Clinical Pharmac

modes.label: Mixed or combined in
modes.description: A small word such as 'in' after mixed or taken, leading into combination or same syringe.
modes.example: The pharmacokinetic parameters of pramlintide are altered when SYMLIN is mixed<< in>> the same syringe with regular, N

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words about a relationship or interaction between two things.
card.plain: It marks the spot where the text is about to say what a drug is combined or mixed with.
